A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same X-GRAAD research work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR and clean-accuracy experiments across multiple models, datasets, and attacks, together with ablations, threshold sensitivity, domain-shift evaluation, and computational costs.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds clean-label and multi-token trigger evaluations in Appendices A.1.2 and A.1.5.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), Algorithm 1, attention-gradient scoring, percentile thresholding, and character-level trigger corruption are unchanged. The new attack scenarios test the existing defense; they do not introduce a new component or adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds clean-label poisoning and multi-token phrase-trigger scenarios on BERT/SST-2. These modestly extend attack coverage beyond v1's evaluated scenarios. The sentiment/topic tasks, three datasets, and existing attacks, including the BadPre domain-shift evaluation, remain.

E2.justification: ONION, RAP, FT, MEFT, and PURE retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. New Table 4 evaluates the same five defenses against phrase triggers. The existing exclusion of PURE for DeBERTa is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added clean-label experiment specifies a 20% poisoning ratio with trigger cf on BERT/SST-2 and reports poisoned-sample accuracy alongside ASR and CACC. The phrase-trigger study adds comparisons with and without defense. Existing splits, training budgets, and 95th/65th-percentile thresholds are unchanged; these are additional protocols, not revisions to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices A.1.2 and A.1.5 add limited robustness tests addressing preserved training labels and multi-token triggers. Figure 6 adds attribution case studies for three phrases. The earlier threshold sensitivity, component ablation, domain-shift test, attribution analyses, and demonstrations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports means over five independent runs, and Figure 4's error bars are unchanged. The added experiments introduce no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information. Appendix A.5's standard-deviation discussion concerns threshold justification, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–3, Figures 1–5, and runtime values are unchanged. The new clean-label test reports undefended-to-defended ASR of 1.0 to 0.012 and CACC of 0.930 to 0.915. New Table 4 reports X-GRAAD ASRs of 0.012, 0.058, and 0.022 for the three phrase triggers, while Figure 6 adds attribution findings. These are additional results, not improvements over corresponding v1 settings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 newly makes the defender's white-box access to parameters, gradients, and attention weights an explicit threat-model assumption. This formalizes access already implicit in the method rather than changing its computations. The mathematical scoring definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same novelty, interpretability, inference-time defense, and effectiveness claims. The appendix additions provide further support without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets phrase-trigger attribution as concentration onto a high-saliency pivot token and extends its applicability discussion to clean-label attacks. Appendix A.5 replaces v1's empirical observation of lower ALBERT scores with an explanation based on shared layers and adds standard-deviation analogies for threshold selection. Defender white-box access is also explicitly qualified.

D1.justification: The added experiments disclose the clean-label trigger cf, its 20% poisoning ratio, and the exact phrases the silver quill, a crimson echo, and james bond. Existing optimizer settings, epoch budgets, hardware, validation fraction, software, and toolkit access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section, bibliography, and novelty positioning are unchanged. New passages reuse already cited works by Cui, Liu, and Zhao to attribute experimental protocols and access assumptions.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Local edits rename Section 5.2.3 from Robustness Analysis to Sensitivity Analysis, clarify defender capabilities, expand Appendix A.5, and insert two appendix subsections. The title's capitalization and formatting also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds the phrase-trigger comparison as Table 4 and a four-panel Figure 6. The old runtime Table 4 becomes Table 5. Existing figures retain their images, with a revised Figure 3 caption and some float relocations. Title formatting and page-header rules also change.

improvement.justification: The new experiments address previously untested clean-label and multi-token trigger cases, and the explicit defender-access assumption clarifies applicability. These provide a limited evidential improvement because the additions remain confined to BERT/SST-2. Appendix A.5 also introduces an unsupported correspondence between percentiles and mean-plus-standard-deviation thresholds, weakening that explanation. Overall, the useful additional validation outweighs this localized weakness.
